title: An additive functor commutes with extension by zero for nonnegative homology
statement: Let D and B be abelian categories [def-sp-abelian], E:D→B an additive functor, K a cochain complex in D indexed by natural numbers, and q a natural number. Extend K to the integers by making every negative term zero. Then the degree-q homology of E applied termwise to this integer extension is isomorphic to degree-q homology of E applied termwise to the original natural-indexed complex. E need not be exact.

source.place: extend.X (41), extend.d (65), extend (118); CategoryTheory/Limits/Preserves/Shapes/Zero.lean: Functor.map_isZero (57); Embedding/ExtendHomology.lean: extendHomologyIso (325).

proof.text: Apply the existing HomologicalComplex.mapExtendIso, which identifies the image under an additive functor of the integer extension of K with the integer extension of the image of K. This canonical isomorphism packages the component and differential checks for the extension-by-zero construction.

Map that complex isomorphism by the degree-q integer homology functor and compose it with HomologicalComplex.extendHomologyIso for embeddingUpNat. The latter includes q=0 and its zero incoming differential, so no exactness of E is required. Expose this explicit composite as mapExtendHomologyIso; the existing Nonempty theorem packages that constructed isomorphism.

proof_origin.note: The duplicate component and complex isomorphisms remain removed. mapExtendHomologyIso directly composes upstream mapExtendIso mapped by homology with extendHomologyIso. The unchanged existence statement packages this canonical construction; no choice of a witness and no remaining holes.

theorem mapExtendHomology_nonempty_iso
    {D : Type u} [Category.{v} D] [Abelian D]
    {B : Type u'} [Category.{v'} B] [Abelian B]
    (E : D ⥤ B) [E.Additive] (K : CochainComplex D ℕ) (q : ℕ) :
    Nonempty
      (((E.mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj
          (K.extend ComplexShape.embeddingUpNat)).homology (q : ℤ) ≅
        ((E.mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℕ)).obj K).homology q)
